findings.title: Removing the whole-function lock allows concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for its entire duration, which (coarsely) serialized index creation. With the lock now only taken around the final map write, two concurrent callers (e.g. two gRPC Search requests hitting getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource, or a watch event arriving during a first search) can both observe GetIndex()==nil and both run BuildIndex for the same key. For file-based indexes both will call bleve.New with the same directory (filepath.Join(Root, namespace, resource.group)); the second call fails or clobbers the first, and the cache ends up with one index while the other caller holds a stale index object that will never receive watch updates. getOrCreateIndex in resource/search.go already has a TODO acknowledging the per-key blocking need; the lock removal makes this a live bug rather than a theoretical one. A per-key singleflight/mutex is needed.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads b.cache without the cache lock while BuildIndex writes it
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no cacheMu protection. BuildIndex now writes to b.cache (b.cache[key] = idx) concurrently with index builds running in parallel from init's errgroup workers. Previously the coarse lock at least serialized map writes across all builds; now an unsynchronized map read concurrent with a map write can panic the process with 'concurrent map read and map write' or return inconsistent totals. Take b.cacheMu.RLock() in TotalDocs.

findings.title: totalBatchesIndexed is incremented from multiple errgroup goroutines without synchronization
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each group.Go closure does totalBatchesIndexed++ on a plain int shared across up to s.initWorkers concurrent goroutines. This is a data race (undefined behavior; the span attribute 'namespaced_indexed' can be wrong). Use sync/atomic or collect counts per goroutine.

findings.title: Goroutine writes to shared err variable raced by main test goroutine
findings.body: The goroutine launched at line 50 assigns to the outer err variable (err = ms.Run()), while the main test goroutine subsequently reads and reassigns the same err at lines 59-62 (client.Get, res.Body.Close) and again in require.NoError. This is a data race that can also cause a require.NoError on line 60 to see the 'context canceled' error set by the goroutine during shutdown, producing flaky failures. Use a local variable inside the goroutine.
